question.value: Can HCN and HNC emission trace heating processes (mechanical vs cosmic-ray) associated with star formation in the NGC 253 CMZ, and what densities and cosmic ray ionization rates characterise its GMCs?

evidence.quote: We analyze HCN and HNC emission in the nearby starburst galaxy NGC 253 to investigate its effectiveness in tracing heating processes associated with star formation.
Our work combines ALCHEMI observations with chemical and physical modeling in order to ascertain the mechanisms driving the high kinetic temperatures in the nucleus of NGC 253.
The ALMA Cycle 5 Large Program ALCHEMI (project code 2017.1.00161.L) imaged the CMZ within NGC 253 in the ALMA frequency Bands 3, 4, 6, and 7.
This survey was subsequently extended to Band 5 during ALMA Cycle 6 (project code 2018.1.00162.S).
The ALMA Cycle 5 Large Program ALCHEMI (project code 2017.1.00161.L) imaged the CMZ within NGC 253 in the ALMA frequency Bands 3, 4, 6, and 7.

claims.hypothesis: HCN/HNC ratio traces strong mechanical heating in the NGC 253 CMZ
claims.experiment: Measure GMC-averaged HCN/HNC intensities and model with UCLCHEM+RADEX; compare with Meijerink+11 predictions; UCLPDR heating
claims.result: Ratios 1-5, abundance ratios <10, far below ~50 expected for significant mechanical heating; CR heating reproduces high T
claims.finding: Cosmic ray heating dominates; mechanical heating not significant for HCN/HNC chemistry

evidence.quote: we find cosmic ray heating dominates the heating budget, and mechanical heating does not play a significant role in the HCN and HNC chemistry

evidence.loc: 4.5 The Effect of Cosmic Rays on the HCN/HNC Ratio
evidence.quote: Thus we conclude that there is little contribution from mechanical heating and that cosmic ray heating alone can produce high kinetic temperatures.
